title: pool-reservation-flow-ux-sketches
content:
Context:
This is a working sketch doc for the Dedicated Capacity console focusing on the reservation flow, burst allocations and autoscale policy editor. Intended audience: console PM, infra SRE, applied-ML (capacity planners), and frontend eng pairing.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- Enable a team or tenant to reserve GPU capacity for a time window with clear visibility into costs and preemption behavior.
- Make bursts (short-term extra capacity) easy to request and approve, and show immediate impact on latency SLOs and billing.
- Reduce support churn by surfacing conflict resolution and alternative suggestions when requested reservations cannot be satisfied.
- Keep UI lightweight for power users (keyboard-first) but discoverable for new users.

Primary personas and journeys (sketches):
1) Platform Engineer (pool owner)
   - Need: allocate capacity to teams, set default autoscale policies, and pre-authorize burst caps.
   - Flow: Pool > Edit policy > Default reservation horizon (30d) > Approve team proposals from queue.
   - Key UI items: policy inline editor, pending proposals list, approve/rollback actions, audit trail link.

2) Product ML Engineer (tenant requesting reservation)
   - Need: secure guaranteed throughput for a model rollout window (3 days) and optionally request burst for a launch spike.
   - Flow: Create reservation wizard -> choose pool -> choose instance profile (p4d, a100-80g) -> select start/end -> choose guaranteed GPUs and soft-burst cap -> review cost impact -> submit.
   - Key UI items: capacity planner card (visual timeline), cost estimator, fallbacks if requested GPUs unavailable.

3) On-call SRE (conflict resolver)
   - Need: quickly see why a reservation failed and propose mitigations: change time, reduce size, use preemptible instances, or schedule across regions.
   - Flow: Reservation conflict alert -> view dependency map -> apply temporary override or notify stakeholders.

Wireframe screens and component notes (visual description):
- Pool Overview (list view)
  - Top strip: pool name, region, HW type badges, live utilization sparkline (last 1h/24h), SLA badge (bronze/silver/gold).
  - Column 1: active reservations (compact chips with user, size, time range). Hover opens compact timeline.
  - Column 2: autoscale policy snippet + edit pencil -> opens modal editor.
  - Column 3: pending proposals queue with approve/deny quick actions.
  - Micro-interaction: clicking a chip opens the Reservation Detail flyout (slide-over) with audit history and cost breakdown.

- Reservation Creation Wizard (multi-step)
  - Step 1: Basic details (name, owner, description) + tagging for billing center.
  - Step 2: Capacity selection (graphical timeline): drag handles to set window, slider to choose GPU count. UI enforces pool max and shows live available capacity overlay.
  - Step 3: Burst options -> radio: none | soft-burst (best-effort) | hard-reserve (requires approval). Explain preemption semantics inline.
  - Step 4: Cost & SLO impact -> estimated token cost / hour, predicted median latency change, expected throttling risk. Button: "Simulate" runs a lightweight check and returns suggestions.
  - Step 5: Review & submit -> shows alternatives if unavailable (shift days, use preemptible nodes, smaller shapes).
  - Error states: if overlapping with an existing hard reserve, block and show conflict resolver link.

- Autoscale Policy Editor (modal)
  - Editor fields: min_gpus, max_gpus, scale_metric (inference_rps, queued_batch_size, tail_latency_p90), scale_window, cooldown.
  - Visual: preview of expected capacity across a representative day (small bar chart).
  - Suggestion helper: UI hints -> "Based on current 7-day pattern, we suggest max=24, min=2, window=5m". Toggle to apply suggestion.
  - Safety: require a confirmation step for policy that allows aggressive scale-down during active reservations.

- Burst Request Modal (lightweight)
  - Fields: burst_size, duration, priority (low/medium/high), justification (free text), auto-approve checkbox (if user has allowance).
  - Preview shows: how burst affects pool utilization and billing delta, which reservations could be impacted.
  - Auto-approval rules: tied to team quota and account spend threshold. Visual indicator if request would consume >80% of team's quota.

- Reservation Detail Flyout
  - Tabs: Overview, Timeline, Audit, Cost, Affected Applications.
  - Timeline: stacked view of reservations + bursts. Hovering on overlapping segments shows conflict origin.
  - Audit: who created, approvals, last modified. Link to the linear ticket or slack thread if present.

Accessibility notes:
- All timeline widgets must expose textual equivalents and keyboard controls for drag/resize.
- Color palette must pass 4.5:1 contrast for important tags (conflict = red).
- Screen-reader text for burst justification and preemption semantics.

Detailed interactions & edge cases (bullet list):
- If user selects hard-reserve and pool lacks capacity, allow "Create waitlist" or propose using a compatible alternate pool (different region or shape).
- Preemptible pools: clearly label cost vs eviction risk; reservation can set "prefer_preemptible:true" to reduce costs but will show eviction probability.
- Partial approvals: approver can reduce GPU count on approval and system notifies requester with an option to accept or cancel.
- Multi-tenant fairness: show a per-tenant credit burn rate for bursts; if a tenant uses >75% of burst credits in 24h, subsequent requests are auto-low-priority.
- Cross-region reservations: allow composite view but require explicit network egress opt-in.

Backlog & grooming items (prioritized):
1. Reservation timeline component (MVP) - 3w - Acceptance: draggable handles, keyboard resize, overlay of availability. Linked: JIRA-ENG-7902.
2. Cost estimator stub (client-side) - 2w - Acceptance: show per-hour estimate, currency and cost center tagging.
3. Burst request flow + auto-approval rules - 2w - Acceptance: modal, quota check, request API integration.
4. Autoscale policy editor (visual preview) - 3w - Acceptance: editor with suggestion toggle, server validation.
5. Conflict resolution UX + suggest alternatives - 2w - Acceptance: block on hard-conflict with actionable suggestions.
6. Reservation audit trail & notification plumbing - 1w - Acceptance: show recent events and email/slack notify.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Billing model: should bursts be billed at a premium multiplier or simply drained from quota? (Finance input needed)
plain_text_preview: Working sketch: reservation wizard + burst modal, policy editor + timeline component. Drafted by Aisha Patel on console-and-tooling. Open items: billing model for bursts, cross-region egress opt-in, partial approval UX. Linked: JIRA-ENG-7821, PR 214.
